_meta.price_note: Prices are reader-reported observations from the page's table and comments, not official data. Always keep the 'observed' date and treat old entries as stale.
_meta.official_tariff_page: http://www.transport.tn/fr/article/110/tarif-du-transport-non-regulier-des-personnes-par-les-voitures-louage (Arabic only; the source says it is out of date but still a good indication)

concept.summary: Louage = shared intercity taxi network. Minibuses run a fixed route and leave when full. Described as one of the most widely used and convenient ways to travel in Tunisia.
concept.vehicle: White minibus/estafette with a red or blue stripe, usually Japanese-made, very high mileage (rarely under 400,000 km).
concept.departure_rule: Departs once all 8 passenger seats are taken (no fixed timetable).
concept.route_signage: Route is shown on a sign on the roof and a card at the rear. Drivers stand in front of the vehicle and shout the destination.
concept.tourist_pricing: Fares are state-regulated and posted in the vehicle; the source says there is no tourist overcharging.

vehicle_types.scope: inter-governorate (big city to big city, e.g. Tunis-Nabeul, Sousse-Sfax)

vehicle_types.note: Can leave half full; drops off and picks up in villages along the way.
Common in the countryside; can be completely full when there is a souk nearby.

operating_hours.advice: Travel in the morning, especially in summer and during Ramadan; avoid returning late.
operating_hours.empty_seat_option: You can pay for the empty seats so the louage leaves, as long as a louage is available for that trip.

stations.general: Every town, and often every village, has one or more louage stations. Easy to spot by watching where louages arrive and depart. Locals and taxi drivers know where they are.
other_stations_mentioned: Yasmine Hammamet (station El Lemdina, bus line 115 stop)

options: Pay the driver directly, often inside the louage at the end of the trip.
Buy at the station counter (guichet): tell the driver first so he holds your seat, go buy the ticket, then give the ticket to the driver.
tickets.tariffs: Set by the state and displayed inside the vehicle.

pricing_rules.rule_of_thumb: About 7 TND per hour of travel.
pricing_rules.example: From Tunis, about 7 TND gets you roughly one hour away: Bizerte, Zaghouan, Hammamet, Nabeul.
pricing_rules.warning: The rule of thumb is rough. Observed fares below range from ~0.7 TND (very short hops) to 40 TND (Tunis-Médenine).

multi_leg_routes.note: Likely a direct louage exists, but go to the station the day before to confirm and reserve.

djerba_notes: Few direct louage links to Djerba.
Leaving Djerba is slow: morning demand exceeds seats, so stations issue queue tickets and groups of 8 leave in turn. Waits of 2-4 hours were reported.
Plan extra time when leaving Djerba in the morning.

tips_for_travelers: Travel in the morning, especially in summer and during Ramadan.
Ask locals or taxi drivers where the station is; everyone knows.
For long or unusual routes (Djerba, the south), go to the station the day before to confirm and reserve.
Check the posted tariff inside the vehicle.
Taking a louage is also a good way to meet and talk with Tunisians.
data_quality_notes: All prices come from readers' comments, not an official source; some entries are from 2015-2019.
Station names are as written on the source page (some are neighborhoods or stops, not formal stations); expect to reconcile them with your existing station seed.
No timetable data exists: departures depend on the vehicle filling up.
The source does not give coordinates for any station.
modeling_notes_not_from_source: Model louage as a 'departs when full' service: show estimated wait/frequency rather than a schedule, with lower confidence in the evening, in summer and during Ramadan.
Store fare observations with their observed date and a confidence or staleness flag, and prefer the newest per route and direction.
Keep louage type (white_red / white_blue / yellow_blue) as an attribute on routes: it determines whether the trip is non-stop and whether it can leave before full.
Represent missing direct links (Kairouan-El Jem, Kairouan-Mahdia, Sfax-Tozeur) as forced transfers in the routing graph.
